A very philosophical and ethical games. Your choices may not affect this person but may affect the others, or even if it doesn't affect those people today, it may affect them days after or in the coming future. 

The story itself is extremely meaningful. It also allows players to truly reflect upon themselves, also think twice on what is correct to do. So are you more to morally or legally? Play the game to find out yourself, hehe! 

Overall, it is a great game to test myself. [spoiler]I actually ended up sacrificing myself to free the Thought but the ending is satisfying; the cycle of peeking and misinterpreting others' personal info finally seem comes to an end, eventually lead to the return of peace to the citizen. These seem to be morally humane, to me.[/spoiler] I really love how this game allows me to reflect upon myself even deeper and testing me upon my decision making in every choices and certain dilemmas. I believe this is good practice on our decision-making skills? Considering we always face these a lot in our lives as well xD

So yes, to those who have not play it - do give it a try! Hehe >w<

8/10 loved digging into people's private lives for hours.

So, you're nobody important. And a nearby country is looking for people like you (not-important foreigners with an Internet access) to offer them a job. So you take it.

Your first task is to make a background check on this girl. She's a suspect, possibly connected to a minor terrorist attack.  So you start digging, but the longer you dig, the messier her story gets. Turns out that the government has some unique tools that will help you find more data - a limited access to the girl's social media. And she is typing with her friend - right now.

You are not making one moral decision after another, you don't try to protect your family and keeps yourself safe. You truly are just an employee. Terrorists killed people. And they want to strike again. And you can stop them... But to do so, you need to completely invade civilians' privacy. Break into the most intimate parts of their lives. And even if you decide it's justifiable, you are more than aware of how abusive the same tools can be. How mishandling them may ruin careers.

But on the other hand... If you quit, people will die. You could have save them, and you won't, it's pretty much you fault. And the deeper you go, the more barriers you have to breach. Even to the point when finding yet another cellphone that you can hack into makes you smile. 

So... What are you going to do?

[h1]Orwell - Keeping an Eye On You - [/h1][spoiler]And you, and you, and you ...[/spoiler]

A great game to let you explore itself and yourself, or to give you the possibility to do things you'd normally never do, or to present you with the realisation that you can never be able to foresee all the consequences (your) actions (judge for yourself to what extent this might apply to thoughts) might have. And you will most probably be able to gain even more insights from spending a few fine hours within this world.

My only criticism is that, in my opinion, the game morally assumes you are nothing but a bad, subjective, judgemental investigator, influenced only by your own goals and preconceptions in the decisions you make. Although the world reacts to your actions, the game itself does not really consider your actions within the overall moral judgement that it passes - but perhaps this is too much to ask from a game already offering such an interesting storyline and such a variety of options.

Have you ever wanted to spy on people, collect mountains of evidence against them for crimes they may (or may not) have committed, and generally be a total creeper online? Well look no further than Orwell, a game where you basically play as Edward Snowden's worst nightmare come to life. 

It's not super complex, it's basically a visual novel with some computer UI prompts and branching choices depending on your actions (or inaction,) but it's a neat concept that is almost fully realized. Just wish this was longer, but there's DLC I might get on a whim one day.

Love how strangely unique the game feels compared to other titles released in the past few years. Feels more like a social adventure than a game and I respect that. Can't wait to see the other chapters for this game.

Orwell: Keeping an Eye On You is an interesting but short game. The gameplay is simple. Point and click to get through the game while you try gathering as much intel about your targets within the Orwell system. There's enough mystery and suspense here to keep you occupied for a couple hours. But by the end of it, I felt a little disappointed that the game wasn't longer. Maybe I completed the story too quickly? But overall, I enjoyed the intriguing plot, the dialogue between characters is entertaining, and the graphics aren't too bad either. I'd recommend it. I look forward to playing the second game.
